concept.name: Alias resolution
concept.definition: The process of mapping non-preferred or variant terms (aliases, abbreviations, synonyms, misspellings) to the canonical concept they denote, using the equivalence relationships of a controlled vocabulary. In ANSI/NISO Z39.19 terms, this applies the USE/UF (used-for) cross-references that link non-preferred terms to preferred terms.
concept.intuition: Whatever name someone uses — 'MACD', 'moving average convergence divergence', 'MACD indicator' — the system figures out they all mean the same concept.
concept.mechanics: A lookup layer maintains alias-to-canonical mappings (exact match, normalization rules for case/punctuation, or learned matching) and rewrites incoming terms before indexing or retrieval. Unresolved aliases are flagged for vocabulary maintenance rather than silently creating duplicate concepts.
concept.failure_modes: Fails on ambiguous aliases that map to different concepts in different contexts (e.g., 'gamma' the option Greek vs. gamma scalping jargon), on unseen aliases, and on false-positive merges of distinct concepts. Pure string matching misses paraphrases; pure embedding matching can over-merge.
concept.misconceptions: Alias resolution is not just string matching or spell-checking — it is a vocabulary governance problem, and an alias table is only as good as its maintenance. Resolving an alias does not resolve the underlying entity in the world (that is entity linking).
concept.example: A user asks about 'VIX futures contango'; alias resolution maps 'VIX' to the canonical concept 'CBOE Volatility Index' and 'contango' to its canonical entry before the answer is composed.

citations.source: ANSI/NISO Z39.19-2005 (R2010), Guidelines for the Construction, Format, and Management of Monolingual Controlled Vocabularies
citations.section: Abstract (NISO publication page; standard defines equivalence relationships between preferred and non-preferred terms)
